prerequisites: It is considered advisable to have studied Physics in high school courses.

learning_outcomes.text: Understanding and mastery of the basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism and their application to solve engineering problems.

syllabus_topics: Magnitudes and Units: Units and Dimensions
Scalar and vector magnitudes: vector algebra
Kinematics: Displacement, velocity and acceleration vectors
Types of motion: Uniform Rectilinear Motion (URM), Uniformly Accelerated Rectilinear Motion (UARM), Uniform Circular Motion (UCM)
Types of force: gravitational, normal, friction, tension
Work and Energy: Definition of work
Conservative and non-conservative forces: Potential energy
Dynamics of systems: Systems of particles and rigid body
Newton's second law for rigid bodies: Moment of inertia and rotational energy
Conservation of linear and angular momentum
Oscillations and waves: Simple harmonic motion
Principle of superposition and interference: standing waves
Density and pressure of a fluid
Fluid Dynamics: Introduction and fundamental concepts
Applications of Bernoulli's equation: Torricelli's Theorem
Fundamentals of thermodynamics: Thermodynamic description of a system
Thermal expansion of solids and liquids
Second law of thermodynamics: Second law of thermodynamics
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.2 * In-class Test + 0.6 * Final Exam + 0.2 * Laboratory Evaluation. To pass, students must actively participate in all lab sessions, obtain a minimum grade of 4 (out of 10) in the final exam, and achieve a final grade of 5 or higher. Only the final exam is re-evaluable in the extraordinary session; the in-class test and laboratory evaluation are not re-evaluable.
